intro: You've searched for a simple will near me, which usually means you want to put a straightforward will in place without travelling far or paying for complexity you don't need. A simple will is often enough to say who gets your money, property and possessions when you die, and to name someone to look after any children. We can introduce you to a wills and probate specialist local to you, and they will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a simple will near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for a simple will near me want a clear, local service for a straightforward estate.
needs: You want to leave your home and savings to your partner or children without creating a trust or other complex arrangement.
You have a straightforward estate and want a will that reflects your wishes, rather than relying on the rules of intestacy.
You want to name substitute beneficiaries in case someone you have chosen dies before you.
You need to know where the original will can be kept safely, and who will hold it.
You would prefer to speak to someone nearby, so meetings and signing are convenient.
context_heading: What to understand about simple wills and regulation
context: Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so not everyone who offers will writing is regulated. Solicitors regulated by the SRA and chartered legal executives regulated by CILEx are insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman, and many specialists are also members of STEP or Solicitors for the Elderly. When you choose someone, ask whether they are regulated, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and where your original will will be stored.

Scotland has its own rules on succession and confirmation, so if you live in Scotland make sure your adviser practises in the right jurisdiction. A simple will can still be appropriate for straightforward estates, but it is worth checking that the person you speak to deals with wills regularly and can explain the process clearly.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for a simple will near you, and mention the area you would like the specialist to cover.
Describe broadly what you own, such as a home, savings or a car, without giving exact figures.
Explain who you want to benefit, for example a partner, children or other chosen people.
Mention whether you have children under eighteen and whether you want to name a guardian.
Say whether you have an existing will or have never made one.
Let us know if you would prefer to meet in person locally or are happy to deal with things another way.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the wills and probate specialist
questions: Are you regulated, and by which body?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Where will my original will be stored, and how can I retrieve it if needed?
What information do you need from me to prepare a simple will?
How will you make sure my will is valid and properly signed?
Can you explain what happens if a beneficiary dies before me?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor to make a simple will?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, because writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales. However, solicitors regulated by the SRA and chartered legal executives regulated by CILEx are insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman, which gives you extra protection.

A simple will usually suits a straightforward estate where you leave assets to a partner, children or chosen people without complex trusts. If your affairs are more complicated, the specialist can tell you what else might be needed.

faqs.q: Why should I name substitute beneficiaries?
faqs.a: If someone you have chosen to benefit dies before you, a substitute beneficiary can step in so that your wishes are still followed. This is a common part of a simple will.

faqs.q: Where should I keep my original will?
faqs.a: It is important to keep the original safe, and many people ask their solicitor or will writer to store it. Always check where it will be held and how you or your executors can get it when needed.

extra_heading: Making your simple will easy to sort out locally
extra: Searching for a simple will near me often means you have been meaning to do this for a while and want it to be as easy as possible. A straightforward will does not need to be complicated, but it does need to be clear, properly signed and kept somewhere safe, so the person you speak to should be able to explain each of those steps in plain terms.

When you compare local options, the distance matters less than what happens at the first appointment. Ask what they need from you beforehand, whether you can meet in person near your home or deal with things another way, and how they will talk you through who should benefit and what happens if someone dies before you. A specialist who deals with wills regularly should be able to set this out clearly without jargon.

It also helps to think about what makes your situation simple in the first place. If you own a home, have savings and want to leave everything to a partner, children or chosen people, a simple will is usually the right place to start, but if you have children under eighteen or want to name substitute beneficiaries, those points are worth raising early so the will reflects them properly.

extra_faqs.q: Is a simple will cheaper than a complex one?
extra_faqs.a: A simple will usually involves less work than one with trusts or business assets, so it is often quoted differently. Because quotes are price on application, ask the specialist to explain what their quote covers before you decide.

extra_faqs.q: Can I make a simple will if I have never made one before?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, and it is a common starting point. Tell the specialist whether you have an existing will or none at all, and they can explain what information they need from you to prepare a simple will.

extra_faqs.q: Does a simple will still need to be signed in a particular way?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, a will must be signed and witnessed correctly to be valid. Ask the specialist to explain the signing and witnessing requirements so your will is not put at risk.
